title: Myopia: increased anterior-posterior globe diameter
vignette: A 14-year-old boy is brought to the clinic by his mother due to changes in vision. For the last few weeks, the patient has been squinting when trying to read the interactive whiteboard in class and has had to sit closer to the front of the room. He has also developed headaches. The patient has no chronic medical conditions and takes no medications. Temperature is 37.2 C (99 F), blood pressure is 116/76 mm Hg, and pulse is 70/min. Examination of the eyes shows equal and reactive pupils. Extraocular muscles are intact, and visual field testing reveals no defects. Visual acuity shows 20/70 in both eyes. His ability to read close text is normal. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms?

clues.text: squinting when trying to read the interactive whiteboard in class
clues.note: Difficulty seeing distant objects (the whiteboard) with squinting is the classic complaint of myopia (nearsightedness).

clues.text: Visual acuity shows 20/70 in both eyes
clues.note: Reduced distance acuity (20/70) with an otherwise normal exam indicates a simple refractive error rather than an ocular disease.

clues.text: His ability to read close text is normal
clues.note: Preserved NEAR vision with blurred DISTANCE vision is characteristic of myopia - the focal point falls in front of the retina for distant objects but near objects still focus correctly.

whatMatters: An adolescent with blurred DISTANCE vision but normal NEAR vision and an otherwise normal eye exam has MYOPIA (nearsightedness). Myopia is most often caused by an INCREASED ANTERIOR-POSTERIOR (axial) DIAMETER of the globe, so the image focuses ANTERIOR to the retina. Answer C.
strategy: Recognize myopia (bad distance vision, good near vision), then recall its cause: an eye that is too long (increased axial length) focuses distant images in front of the retina. Corrected with a diverging (concave) lens. Reject 'image focused posterior to retina' (that's hyperopia), loss of lens accommodation (presbyopia, age >40), chronically increased IOP (glaucoma), and visual cortex maldevelopment (amblyopia).

options.text: Disturbance in development of the visual cortex
Increased anterior-posterior diameter of the eyes
Loss of accommodating power of the lens
Refracted image focused posterior to the retina

eliminations.label: Chronically increased IOP - glaucoma
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: sustained high intraocular pressure causing optic neuropathy (glaucoma). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: glaucoma causes progressive PERIPHERAL field loss and optic cupping, not isolated blurred distance vision with normal fields in a teen. ✅ Correct if: peripheral vision loss with optic cupping/high IOP.

eliminations.label: Visual cortex maldevelopment - amblyopia
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: cortical suppression of one eye's input (amblyopia), often from untreated strabismus. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this patient has symmetric, recent-onset reduced acuity correctable as a refractive error, not developmental cortical suppression. ✅ Correct if: unilateral decreased acuity from childhood strabismus/deprivation.

eliminations.label: Loss of lens accommodation - presbyopia (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: age-related loss of lens elasticity/accommodation (presbyopia), impairing NEAR vision, typically after age 40. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this 14-year-old has impaired DISTANCE vision with normal near vision - the opposite pattern and wrong age. ✅ Correct if: an older adult with blurred near vision needing reading glasses.

eliminations.label: Image focused posterior to retina - hyperopia
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a refracted image falling BEHIND the retina, from a short/low-power eye = hyperopia (farsightedness). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: hyperopia blurs NEAR vision; this patient's problem is DISTANCE vision, indicating the image falls ANTERIOR to the retina (myopia). ✅ Correct if: blurred near vision corrected by a converging (convex) lens.

reasoning: Blurred distance vision + normal near vision + otherwise normal eye exam = myopia
Myopia is usually due to an eye that is too long (increased axial/anterior-posterior diameter)
A long eye focuses distant images ANTERIOR to the retina, blurring distance vision
mechanism: Myopia (nearsightedness) is a refractive error in which parallel light rays from DISTANT objects are focused ANTERIOR to (in front of) the retina, so distant objects appear blurred while near objects (whose rays diverge and focus farther back) remain clear. The most common cause is an increased ANTERIOR-POSTERIOR (axial) length of the globe - the eye is 'too long' for its refractive power. New-onset myopia peaks during the adolescent growth spurt as the eye elongates rapidly (risk higher with a positive family history or East Asian descent). It is corrected with a diverging (concave) lens that moves the focal point back onto the retina. Contrast hyperopia (farsightedness): a short eye focuses the image POSTERIOR to the retina, blurring near vision, corrected by a converging (convex) lens. Presbyopia is an age-related loss of lens accommodation affecting near vision (after ~40), glaucoma is optic neuropathy from elevated IOP, and amblyopia is cortical suppression - none fits this teen's isolated blurred distance vision.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Ophtho > refractive errors: myopia = long eye (increased axial length), image anterior to retina, concave lens; hyperopia = short eye, image posterior, convex lens; presbyopia = lens accommodation loss.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Blurred distance + clear near vision localizes the focal point ANTERIOR to the retina = myopia (long globe).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on myopia vs hyperopia, axial length, accommodation, concave vs convex lens, or presbyopia? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Image POSTERIOR to retina = hyperopia; accommodation loss = presbyopia (near vision, older); IOP = glaucoma; cortex = amblyopia.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: myopia = eye too long -> image in front of retina -> blurred distance vision; correct with concave (diverging) lens.

keywords.back: Increased anterior-posterior (axial) length of the globe

keywords.front: Where the image focuses in myopia
keywords.back: Anterior to the retina (corrected with concave lens)
